sites.name: Ba Den Mountain
sites.event: Known as the 'Roof of the Southeast' (986m), associated with the legend of Linh Son Thanh Mau (Ba Den) and the revolutionary movement.

sites.name: Tay Ninh Holy See
sites.event: The ancestral temple of Cao Dai religion, a unique religious architectural work harmoniously combining Asian and Western arts.

sites.name: Dau Tieng Lake
sites.event: The largest artificial irrigation lake in Southeast Asia at the time of construction, stretching across 3 provinces (mainly in Tay Ninh).

place.commune: Phuoc Minh, Phuoc Ninh, Suoi Da Communes...

sites.name: Relic of the Central Office for South Vietnam Base
sites.event: Known as the 'Resistance Capital' or 'R', the residence and workplace of the southern revolutionary headquarters during the anti-American war.

sites.name: Binh Thanh Ancient Tower
sites.event: The only Cham Pa ancient tower (belonging to the Oc Eo culture) in the Southern region that still retains relatively intact stone walls, dating back to the 8th-9th centuries.

sites.name: Lo Go - Xa Mat National Park
sites.event: An ASEAN Heritage Park, conserving many typical ecosystems of the transition zone between the Southeast and the Central Highlands.

place.commune: Tan Binh, Tan Lap, Hoa Hiep, Thanh Tay Communes

sites.name: Ma Thien Lanh Valley
sites.event: Likened to the 'Da Lat of the East', this pristine valley is adjacent to three mountains (Ba Den, Phung Mountain, Heo Mountain).

sites.name: Tua Hai Victory Relic
sites.event: The site of the opening battle for the armed Dong Khoi movement in the South (on January 26, 1960).

sites.name: Go Ken Pagoda (Thien Lam Pagoda)
sites.event: An ancient pagoda over 100 years old, where Most Venerable Thich Tu Phong once served as abbot and which is associated with the early formation of the Cao Dai religion.

sites.name: Moc Bai International Border Gate
sites.event: The largest land border gate in the South on the Vietnam - Cambodia border.

sites.name: Chot Mat Tower
sites.event: One of the few ancient towers of the Oc Eo culture remaining in the Southern region, discovered in the early 20th century.
